idiom_name: lambda closure over a Func<...>/Action<...> delegate
implementation_notes: A C# lambda that references its enclosing scope compiles to a delegate plus a compiler-generated closure class holding the captured locals, so `Func<int, int> add5 = y => Add(5, y);` is the entire realisation and the classic binder type has no counterpart in the language. Delegates (Func<...>, Action<...>) are the currency of callbacks, LINQ operators and DI factories, so a specialised delegate is a first-class value there; where a provider must inspect or translate the function (LINQ to SQL) the same lambda is written as Expression<Func<...>>, which is data rather than a closure and cannot hold a statement body. C# 12 lambda default parameters and params collections cover the call-site specialisation case, which is why curried APIs stay rare.
pitfalls: Closures capture variables, not values: a for-loop variable is a single slot for the whole loop (foreach became per-iteration in C# 5), so a specialisation created inside the loop can bind the last value.
A delegate stored on an event or in a long-lived table keeps its closure alive, and the closure keeps everything it references alive - the classic event-handler leak.
Method-group and lambda conversions allocate a delegate each time they are converted; in hot paths hoist the specialised delegate into a field or a static readonly value.
